transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thank you so much for seeing me. Well, I guess what brings me in is this... this constant restless feeling I’ve been dealing with. It’s honestly been driving me a bit crazy lately. It’s like I’m just wound way too tight, all the time, and I absolutely cannot fully settle. 

And it’s incredibly frustrating because it happens even when I’m in situations where I’m really supposed to be calmly sitting. Like at work—I’m a wholesale buyer, so I have these long, intensive planning meetings where we're going over seasonal inventory and vendor contracts for hours, and I just feel this physical hum inside me, like I need to jump out of my chair and pace around the room. I mean, I'm 51, you'd think I'd be used to sitting through a meeting by now! 

But it’s not even just at work, which is the worst part. I try so hard to unwind on my own time. I’ve tried painting, I try doing yoga—which everyone always says is so great for relaxing and finding your center—but even then, when I'm on the mat in a quiet room, or sitting with my brushes trying to focus on a canvas, I can't just *be*. I can't settle into it. My body just won't relax, and I end up feeling almost more agitated because I'm trying to force myself to be calm and it just isn't working. It's like I have this internal motor that just won't shut off, no matter what I'm doing or how desperately I just want to sit still for five minutes.
Have you started or changed the dose of any new medications recently, such as antipsychotics or other prescription drugs?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't started any new medications at all, and definitely no antipsychotics or anything major. I'm actually really careful about what I take, to be honest. I mean, if you looked in my medicine cabinet right now, it’s basically just... well, maybe some ibuprofen for when I get a headache from staring at vendor contracts on my screen for too long, and a daily multivitamin that I probably only remember to take maybe three days out of the week anyway. 

But as far as actual prescriptions go? No, no changes, no new doses. I’ve always been the type of person who is a bit hesitant to just jump on a new medication unless it's absolutely necessary, you know? I like to know exactly what's going into my body. So I really haven't added anything new to my routine lately. It's just... this whole restless feeling is happening entirely on its own. Honestly, I kind of wish I *could* just blame it on a side effect of some new pill, because then at least I’d have an easy answer, right? I could just stop taking it, or switch to something else, and I could go back to normal. But no, I haven't taken anything new.

Along with this physical restlessness, have you also been experiencing a lot of excessive worry or anxious thoughts about various things in your life, like work, health, or family, that are hard to control?

No, actually, not at all. And it’s funny you ask that, because I feel like people always assume that if you can’t sit still, you must be secretly agonizing over something, right? Like, my husband will see me pacing around the living room or fidgeting during a movie, and he'll immediately say, "What's wrong? Are you worried about the kids?" or "Are you stressing over that big vendor contract?" 

But the truth is, I'm really not. I mean, sure, my job is demanding—when you're a wholesale buyer, there's always a lot of money on the line with seasonal inventory, and the shipping logistics alone can be a massive headache. But I'm not *anxious* about it. I know what I'm doing, I have my spreadsheets, I've been doing this for years. I don't sit around chewing my nails over work. And my family is doing great, my health is fine... I don't have this running loop of worst-case scenarios in my head at all. I'm not lying awake at night fretting about things I can't control. 

My mind isn't spinning with fears or worried thoughts, it's really just... it's purely physical. It’s like my brain is totally fine, calm even, but my body is the thing that's acting like it just drank ten cups of coffee. So, no, I wouldn't say I have any of that excessive worry you're talking about. I'm actually a pretty upbeat, practical person when it comes to dealing with life stuff, which is honestly why this whole not-being-able-to-physically-relax thing is so completely baffling and annoying to me!
Did you notice this kind of restlessness and difficulty settling down back when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that started more recently in your adult life?

Oh, gosh, no, this is definitely not a new thing. Not at all. I mean, if I really sit back and think about it... it’s been there my whole life. I honestly can't remember a time when I wasn't like this, to be perfectly frank. My mother used to joke that I was born with a motor attached to me. 

I remember way back in elementary school—and this is going back a ways, obviously—but I clearly remember getting notes sent home to my parents. Just, so many notes from my teachers. They would always write about how I kept popping out of my seat during lessons. Like, we'd be doing a worksheet or something where we were supposed to be quietly working at our desks, and I just physically could not stay in that little plastic chair. I'd be up sharpening my pencil for the fifth time, or walking over to the window, or just standing up at my desk for no reason at all. 

And it wasn't just the moving around, either, it was the talking. I was always talking over my classmates. We'd be having a group discussion and I would just jump right in and interrupt whoever was speaking. I was just so... propelled, I guess? I would even rush to answer questions before the teacher had even finished asking them. Like, they'd get halfway through a sentence and I'd just blurt out the answer because I just couldn't hold it in. It was like the thought was just bubbling up and it had to come out right that second, I couldn't even wait for them to finish their thought. 

My parents were always having to sit me down and talk about waiting my turn and having patience, but it was just so incredibly hard for me to actually do it. So, yeah, I guess I took the long way around to answer your question, but no, this isn't some new mid-life development. It’s really always been exactly like this. It just feels a little more embarrassing now that I'm a fifty-one-year-old woman in a corporate boardroom instead of a kid in a third-grade classroom, you know? But the actual internal feeling is exactly the same.
